title: Prompt Constellations — sketchbook of a reusable prompt fabric
content:
Context and intent:
A lightweight user-facing and runtime pattern for composing small, named prompt fragments (instructions, formatters, safety guards, example blocks, domain facts) that can be re-used, versioned, and fast-swapped at inference time. Working name: "Prompt Constellations". Goal: reduce prompt drift, enable targeted A/B and per-customer tuning, and make provenance + A/B analytics visible in Console.

Why different from current snippets/templating:
- Snippets are ad-hoc blobs; constellations are structured, addressable, and have runtime constraints (max tokens, pinned model variants, quantization-safe).
- Each fragment carries metadata: owner, version, evaluation set, safety tags, golden examples, preferred placement (prefix/suffix/in-context-example), and token budget.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want to assemble a conversation prompt by selecting named fragments so I can reuse the same onboarding text across features and ensure consistent persona tone.
- As an SRE, I want fragments to expose a token budget and cost-estimate so routing can choose cheaper model variants when budget is tight.
- As a data reviewer, I want to see the constellation versions used for any request in tracing so I can debug regressions.
- As an experimenter, I want to A/B two fragments for the same slot without redeploying model or changing code.

Core primitives (first pass):
- Fragment: id, name, content, tags, token_budget, placement_hint (prefix|suffix|example|tool), pinned_models, safety_flags, owner, created_at, version_tag.
- Constellation: ordered list of fragment ids + optional inline overrides (small variable map). Constellations can be versioned and pinned to APIs/routes.
- Runtime resolver: expands constellation to a final prompt respecting token quotas, placement hints, and fallback fragments when pinned model unavailable.

API sketch (informal):
- POST /v1/fragments (create)
- GET /v1/fragments/:id (fetch metadata+content)
- POST /v1/constellations (create composition)
- POST /v1/generate with { constellation_id, overrides, token_budget } -> runtime resolves and scales batch/route choices.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UX: create fragment, compose constellation, attach to a test route in Console (manual).
- Runtime: server expands constellation deterministically and logs fragment ids+versions in trace.
- Metrics: show per-fragment token counts in the token breakdown UI.

Experiment plan:
1) Internal dogfood on ChatOps: convert onboarding primer into fragments (persona, constraints, 3 examples). Run for 1 week, collect conversational quality delta and token delta.
2) A/B test: swap a single fragment (closing instruction) between two variants across 10k requests. Evaluate user engagement and hallucination rate on small eval set.
3) Cost experiment: pin cheaper model variant for one fragment slot and measure CPU/GPU savings and quality regressions.

Open questions / risks:
- Complexity leak: will product teams create huge numbers of fragments leading to discovery and governance problems? Need tagging, ownership policies and pruning tools.
- Security: fragments may contain secrets accidentally. Need linting/scan for PII/API keys and a publish workflow (draft->review->publish).
- Performance: fragment resolution must be O(n) and cheap; must avoid token re-serialization overhead and ensure KV cache reuse for repeated prefixes.
- Compatibility with tool-calling & structured output: how do we ensure fragments that rely on tool outputs remain composable?

Initial instrumentation to add:
- Trace fields: fragment_ids, fragment_versions, resolved_prompt_length, pre/post token counts per fragment, pinned_model_used.
- Console: filter by fragment id to see request funnel and quality metrics.

Next steps (todo):
- Align with Console owners to prototype a minimal compose UI (drag fragments into slots). (owner: Julian)
- Draft a tiny Linear epic for backend primitives + schema (owner: me).
- Quick internal eval set (10–20 prompts) to measure sensitivity to small fragment swaps.

Notes to self (scrap):
- Think about a "fragment contract" for expected outputs (e.g., "final instruction returns JSON with field x"). Could enable compile-time checks in prompt lint.
- Consider cheap caching: if constellation root prefix repeated, store prefix embedding/kv to skip re-tokenizing for subsequent calls.

Random ideas:
- Allow fragments to expose a "confidence multiplier" used by routing to lift latency SLOs when high-quality fragments are present. Kind of like a QoS hint.
- Marketplace of vetted community fragments (curated safety-first fragments) that customers can import and fork.

End of sketch — rough, messy. Want to keep this light and iterate after a convo with Console + Runtime folks.
